question: On real multi-LUN traffic, how differently do Zone, Zone + work stealing and Non-Zone feed one shared FIFO reader queue, and how does that depend on zone imbalance and on the per-request read overhead?
trace: Fujitsu SYSTOR'17 VDI, 2016-02-22 07-20 JST, LUNs 0,1,2,3,4,6, reads only (README hour-change loss dropped)
library: 640 slots (8 rows x 80), 1 TB platters, 1 reader, 8 shuttles, FIFO read-ahead queue K=8, no cache, B1 Silica scheduler, contention hold 0.5 s

placements.contig_1tb: natural: each LUN written sequentially, platters at random rack positions (one zone gets ~36% of reads all day)
placements.contig_balanced: same sequential platters spread so every zone gets ~12.5% of the day's reads; only short-term imbalance remains (busiest zone > 25% in 13% of 10-min windows)
placements.random_1gib: every 1 GiB extent on a random platter: no zone imbalance, little locality

ws_params.note: Silica's thresholds are not public; same defaults as the earlier hotspot study

load_note: arrival rate = 0.75 x Zone's throughput with all requests at t=0, per placement and overhead; the same arrivals are given to all three dispatch policies
